doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Emotional effect of the war and teammates Eddie Jason and Tony
summary: Budd enjoyed the work, and recalls his team members and lifelong friendship with Tony.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Gee. Did it wear on you emotionally?

No I don’t think so. I was really excited. I was delighted. I thought I liked it. The people I was with were so great, the team. And those young men, the two guys, Eddie Jason was one, I haven’t seen him. He’s dead since then. But he came from Providence, Rhode Island. And he probably was a mechanic or salesman or something, and probably about 25 years old. Eddie Jason was his name. And he was just a marvelous little guy. The other fellow was Tony — I’ve forgotten it now, but I got in touch with him. Jason died not long after the war, some influenza or something. But Tony, he still lives and he was just about four years younger than I was. He was in his 30’s. I was about 35, he was about 31. And I kept in touch with him all the rest of his life. He finally settled in Nevada, in Carson City, the Capital of Nevada. I used to hear from him at Christmas, and he’d tell me how he was doing. As a matter of fact, I shouldn’t brag, but when I was installed as President of the AMA, I had written to him and he showed up to that thing, and what a joy to see him. I hadn’t seen him in about 50 years. And my son met him and he was just a marvelous, marvelous guy. And since then he died, and I’ve had notes from his children, how much he thought of me and how much they miss him. And some of the experiences like that, they’re just accidents, I’ve had so much good luck I can’t believe it. And the chance that I happened to see you. You happened to be talking to somebody, and I says there is somebody who likes music, and I tried to strike a conversation without butting in, and I found that you were. And I didn’t come looking to you for anything, it was just that I thought it was somebody who likes music.
Same here. You can tell when you’re in those kind of gatherings you know...
